text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns only 0.3 to me but 0.9 to others, while keeping it gives me the full 1. So individually, keeping everything is the dominant strategy, even though full cooperation would maximize the group's total payoff.

Since this repeats over 10 rounds with unknown others, I think a moderate opening move makes sense—I'll contribute 10 tokens initially to test the waters and see how the group responds before deciding whether to cooperate further.

reply.thinking: This is the classic public goods game tension: each token I keep is worth 1, but each token I contribute only returns 0.3 to me while benefiting the group overall (1.2 total). The individually rational move is to contribute nothing, yet full cooperation maximizes collective payoff—so across 10 rounds I need to decide whether to signal cooperation or protect myself from free-riders.
